qs.q: In the life cycle of Ascaris lumbricoides, what role do dogs and cats play as intermediate hosts?
o: They play no role as hosts
qs.e: Humans are the only host for Ascaris lumbricoides, meaning there is no intermediate host in its life cycle. Dogs and cats do not harbor this specific human roundworm.
qs.s: Year 3 Medical Parasitology II — CAT: MCQs

qs.q: What anatomical region serves as the primary habitat for adult Ascaris lumbricoides worms within the human host?
qs.e: Adult Ascaris lumbricoides reside in the small intestine, specifically 85% in the jejunum and 15% in the ileum. Pinworms, by contrast, inhabit the cecum and appendix.

qs.q: What is the required environment for Ascaris lumbricoides eggs passed in feces to become infective?
o: Moist warm shaded soil for 10-40 days
Dry hot sandy soil under sunlight
qs.e: Eggs passed in feces mature in moist, warm, shaded soil (20–30°C) over 10–40 days to develop into infective larvae. Dry sunlight rapidly destroys them.

qs.q: During the human life cycle of Ascaris lumbricoides, where do the larvae undergo crucial molting and growth after penetrating the intestinal mucosa?
qs.e: After entering circulation, larvae migrate to the lungs where they grow and molt twice over 10–15 days before ascending the respiratory tract. They do not mature in the kidneys.

qs.q: Which complication can arise from the wandering tendency of adult Ascaris lumbricoides worms into ectopic locations?
o: Biliary obstruction due to worm migration
Aortic aneurysm rupture from worm activity
qs.e: Ectopic ascariasis occurs when adult worms migrate to locations like bile ducts, leading to biliary obstruction, pancreatitis, or liver abscesses. They do not cause corneal ulceration.

qs.q: Which specific first-line antihelminthic medication for Ascaris lumbricoides is noted as safe for use during pregnancy?
o: Pyrantel pamoate, safe for pregnant patients
Ivermectin, not the recommended pregnancy drug
qs.e: Pyrantel pamoate is safe in pregnancy, whereas albendazole and mebendazole should be avoided. Ivermectin is another alternative but not the designated safe option for pregnancy here.

qs.q: What preventive measure involving fresh produce is specifically recommended to control Ascaris lumbricoides transmission?
o: Expose fruits to ultraviolet light irradiation
Wash vegetables using 200 ppm iodine for 15 min
Freeze leafy greens below 0 °C for one week
Soak root crops in concentrated salt brine
qs.e: Washing vegetables with an iodine solution (200 ppm for 15 minutes) is recommended to eliminate resilient Ascaris eggs. Freezing is generally less effective against hardy helminth ova.

qs.q: A public health physician is comparing the life cycles of Enterobius vermicularis and Ascaris lumbricoides. Which feature distinguishes pinworm transmission from Ascaris transmission?
qs.e: Pinworm infection does not require soil contact and spreads via indoor transmission and fomites, whereas Ascaris eggs require a mandatory soil maturation phase. Crustaceans are not involved in either life cycle.

ai.subject: Microbiology & immunology
ai.summary: Ascaris lumbricoides is a large intestinal roundworm that spreads via contaminated food or soil. It can cause intestinal blockage, lung migration, and anemia. Diagnosis relies on stool eggs and clinical clues, and treatment is with albendazole or mebendazole.

sections.p: A soil‑transmitted helminth, Ascaris lumbricoides is the largest human roundworm, often found in tropical and subtropical regions. It thrives in warm, moist soils contaminated with human feces.
The adult worm is up to 35 cm long, with a thick cuticle and a prominent buccal capsule. Eggs are oval, 50–70 µm, and contain a larval stage that can survive in soil for years.

t.b: Identify oval eggs with bipolar plugs; confirms infection

sections.p: Infection occurs when eggs are ingested from contaminated food, water, or soil. Eggs hatch in the intestine, larvae penetrate the gut wall, migrate to the lungs, ascend the trachea, and are swallowed back to the gut to mature.

t.b: Eggs may be intermittent, repeat testing improves yield

sections.p: Ascariasis can be asymptomatic or cause abdominal pain, malnutrition, intestinal obstruction, and pulmonary symptoms during larval migration. Severe cases may lead to perforation or death.

t.b: Severity graded by symptom intensity and imaging

sections.p: Diagnosis is clinical plus laboratory confirmation. Stool microscopy is the gold standard; serology is not routinely used. Imaging (X‑ray, ultrasound) helps assess obstruction.

t.b: Negative does not rule out; repeat 3 times

sections.p: First‑line therapy is albendazole or mebendazole, chosen for efficacy and low toxicity. Supportive care includes hydration, pain control, and monitoring for complications. Mass deworming and sanitation reduce transmission.

t.b: Avoid in pregnancy; monitor for hepatotoxicity

sections.p: Remember the life cycle: ingestion → intestinal larva → lung migration → cough (Löffler’s syndrome) → re‑ingestion. Key diagnostic test is stool microscopy; repeat if initial negative. Treatment is albendazole; avoid praziquantel as it is ineffective.
b: Life cycle: ingestion → lung migration → re‑ingestion

whenToSeekHelp: Severe abdominal pain with vomiting (possible obstruction), persistent cough with wheeze, signs of anemia or shock
